messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm running offline replays to validate the new queue-throttle token-budget heuristic. Using Feb traces (prod-2026-02-14). Need an A/B harness comparing control vs new flow. Goals: keep p95 <= 220ms and reduce token cost by ~8-12%. Anyone want to pair?

sam: I'm in. Do we have the sim config? I'll start a run on gpu-sim-3.

maya: config below:
```json
{
  "trace_path": "/mnt/traces/prod-feb-14.jsonl",
  "replayer": "trace_replayer_v2",
  "queue_policy": "new_token_budget",
  "token_budget": 256,
  "kv_warmup": true,
  "batch_formation": "elastic",
  "runtime_profile": true
}
```

jin: heads-up — kernel selection interacts badly with token_budget when seq_len > 1024. In a previous replay we saw fallback to aten kernels for some layers which spiked tail latency. For these replays we should force the kernel-probe stage: `--force-probe=true`.

perf-bot: perf-scan finished for trace prod-feb-14: avg_tokens_per_req=84, pct_long_reqs(>1024)=4.6%, kv_hit_rate=0.72. Attached: /artifacts/1768503333/prof-epoch1.html

aaron: For the A/B harness capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, avg cost per 1M tokens, cache_miss_penalty(ms), kernel_fallback_rate, and %batches exceeding token_budget. Also log batch_size distribution and per-route sample traces.

maya: agreed. Plan: two cohorts — control (token_budget=128, queue_policy=fill_or_timeout) vs experiment (token_budget=256, elastic batcher + kv_warmup). Each replay runs for 4h.

sam: started control run on sim-node-07: `./replay --config control.json --out ./out/control`

maya: started experiment run on sim-node-08: `./replay --config experiment.json --out ./out/exp --force-probe=true`

perf-bot: control run completed: p95=238ms, p99=540ms, avg_cost=$12.4 per 1M tokens, kv_hit_rate=0.68, kernel_fallback_rate=0.9%

perf-bot: experiment run completed: p95=212ms, p99=490ms, avg_cost=$11.1 per 1M tokens, kv_hit_rate=0.75, kernel_fallback_rate=2.1%

jin: interesting — p95 improved and cost dropped, but p99 still high and kernel_fallback_rate doubled. That suggests the probe is picking fast kernels for most batches but failing catastrophically on long-context batches. Need per-request flamegraphs for the long tails.

maya: attaching artifacts: /artifacts/1768503333/exp-flame.svg and /artifacts/1768503333/waterfall-001.png. Waterfall shows several long KV miss stalls around token 1024 boundary.

aaron: propose a 3rd run: token_budget=192, kv_warmup=true, adaptive_probe=true (probe only when median_seq > 512). Hypothesis: we keep cost wins and reduce p99 regressions by avoiding aggressive probing on mixed seq workloads.

sam: +1. I'll queue that. Also let's add per-route traces (1% sampling) — I suspect the long-chat route is the culprit.

maya: added per-route sampling and started run on sim-node-09. Command: 
```bash
./replay --config third.json --out ./out/third --adaptive-probe=true --route-sample=0.01
```

qa-bot: note: experiment run triggered a perf-regression alert (>10% p99 increase relative to baseline). Created ticket INF-783 and attached perf artifacts.

maya: thanks QA — I'll add replay configs, raw traces, and profiling HTML to INF-783.

jin: long-term thought: change kernel-selection policy to prefer stable kernels (slightly lower peak throughput) when seq_len > 1024 to avoid fallback penalties. Also consider making kernel fallback threshold a runtime knob per-model.

aaron: another lever is increasing KV prefetch window for models with conversational history; small increases in kv_hit_rate correlated with lower p95 in the experiment artifacts. Worth testing +prefetch=64 vs +prefetch=128.

maya: closing the loop for now: I'll consolidate A/B metrics and attach a short write-up. If the third run keeps p95 <220ms and cost savings >=8% without an unacceptable p99 regression, we'll promote the heuristic to staging and run a small canary.

sam: sounds good — keep us posted :thumbsup:
